name: kimwitu++
why: A term-rewriting tree processor from the compiler toolkit era, obscure and a little old-school strange.

brief.what_it_is: Kimwitu++ is a meta tool for processing trees (terms), used mainly to generate software, especially compilers. It has its own input language for defining a tree structure and functions that operate on the tree. From that input it generates a set of C++ files, which are then compiled and bound into a program with a C++ compiler. It is the successor to Kimwitu and is licensed under the GNU GPL v2 or later.
brief.why_it_exists: The project page presents it as a tool for building compilers, where a parser (for example lex and yacc) handles the grammar and Kimwitu++ builds the abstract syntax tree that later passes work on. Its successor relationship to Kimwitu is the only other framing the page gives.
brief.how_it_works: Kimwitu++ offers two mechanisms for processing the tree: unparse rules, for code generation, and rewrite rules, for transformations. Each rule is tailored to a node structure by pattern matching, and all rules are applied to the tree recursively. Views let different rules apply to the same kind of node in different contexts, C++ code can be embedded in rules, and a C++ class is generated for each node type that users can extend with their own methods.
brief.install_notes: The page gives no install steps. It says the project is distributed through the Savannah Download Area and that development uses CVS on Savannah. It also says the project needs a C++ compiler to build the generated files. No runtime, account, or first-run configuration is described.
brief.standout: Instead of being a library, it is a generator: a small input language describes the tree and its operations, and it emits C++ classes with pattern-matched rewrite and unparse rules. Its pairing with lex and yacc places it in the classic compiler-toolkit lineage, which is far from most current tooling.
brief.status: The Savannah page lists the development status as 5 - Production/Stable. The most recent news item is dated 9 Feb 2008, and the last news post before that was from 2003. The bug tracker shows 15 open items out of 78 total, and the page lists four members, with Martin v. Loewis and Michael Piefel as group admins. The status is best described as quiet, not abandoned, since the bug tracker is still in use, but the lack of recent news suggests slow activity. I did not check for a recent release.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the Savannah project summary, not a documentation site, so I could not see usage examples or a README with commands. I did not follow any links beyond it, so the actual download, manual, and release history are unverified. The Savannah page notes the project is 'not part of the GNU Project' even though the license is GPL. The news shows the home page and CVS moved to Savannah in 2008, so older links may be stale. Build details and supported platforms are not described on this page.
quotes: Kimwitu++ is the successor to Kimwitu. Like Kimwitu, it is a tool for processing trees (i.e. terms).
Kimwitu++ can be used for generating software - especially when building compilers.
For processing the tree, Kimwitu++ supports two mechanisms: unparse rules (for code generation), and rewrite rules (for transformations).
